title: Update client: check, download, verify, apply
goal: Safely update a Centcom installation: check a release channel, download the artifact for this platform, verify hash and Ed25519 signature, and apply it atomically with rollback, refusing anything unverifiable.
scope_in: Manifest client: GET /v1/releases/{channel}/latest?platform=<linux|darwin|win32>&arch=<x64|arm64> and GET /v1/releases/{channel}/manifest.json for `channel` in `stable|beta|nightly`; validate against schemas/release-manifest.schema.json via C003; read the minimum supported version.

Version logic: semver compare; update only to a higher version on the same channel (downgrade only with explicit `--rollback` to the saved previous binary); channel switch is explicit; honour `min_client_version` from the manifest and `/v1/status`, and the `client_too_old` (HTTP 426 / WS 4426) signal as 'update required'.

Download: streamed to a temp file in the install directory with resume (HTTP Range) on interruption, size cap taken from the manifest `size` (abort if more bytes arrive), 10 s connect and 60 s idle timeouts, progress callbacks.

Verification before any apply: SHA-256 equals the manifest value (constant-time compare), Ed25519 signature over the manifest-defined message verifies against the embedded release public key set (supports 2 keys for rotation) in `keys.ts`; failure deletes the temp file.

Apply: for standalone binaries (Node SEA) atomic replace via rename in the same directory, keep previous as `centcom.prev` for rollback, Windows rename-away-then-move for a running exe, restart hint; for npm/Homebrew installs detect the install method and print the right command instead of self-modifying.

Scheduling: background check at most once per 24 h at startup (ETag cached, non-blocking, 5 s timeout), opt-out via config `update.check=false` / env `CENTCOM_NO_UPDATE_CHECK=1`, emits an `update-available` event (state name `update-available`).
scope_out: Building, signing and publishing artifacts, version/changeset tooling: lane C012; installer packaging: lane C094; auto-update UX integration and channels in the UI: lane C095.
The release CDN and manifest generation (real backend and release process).
Delta/binary-diff updates (full artifact only in v1).
build_against: the mock backend (lane C007): REST from OpenAPI plus the WebSocket relay simulator, started in-process with `startMockBackend()` from @centcom/testkit; no real backend is needed for the manifest endpoints, plus a local static artifact server in @centcom/testkit that serves signed fixture binaries (valid, wrong hash, bad signature, truncated, oversized) produced with a test key; the production public keys are never used in tests (injectable key set).
interfaces: `new UpdateClient(o: { http: HttpClient; currentVersion: string; platform: NodeJS.Platform; arch: string; channel: Channel; keys: ReleaseKeySet; installDir: string; clock; fs: FsLike })`

`check(): Promise<{ available: boolean; version?: string; channel: Channel; notesUrl?: string; required: boolean }>`; `download(o?: { onProgress?: (p: { received: number; total: number }) => void; signal?: AbortSignal }): Promise<StagedUpdate>`; `verify(s: StagedUpdate): Promise<void>`; `apply(s: StagedUpdate): Promise<{ restartRequired: boolean; previous: string }>`; `rollback(): Promise<void>`
CLI: `centcom update [--check] [--channel stable|beta|nightly] [--yes] [--rollback] [--json]`; exit codes 0 up to date or updated, 1 failure, 10 update available (with `--check`)
`ReleaseKeySet = { keys: { id: string; publicKey: string /* base64url Ed25519 */ }[] }` exported from keys.ts (production keys filled by lane C012's signing procedure)
acceptance: `check()` with the mock advertising a higher version returns `available:true`; equal or lower returns false; a pre-release on `stable` is ignored; `--channel beta` requests `/v1/releases/beta/latest` with the right `platform` and `arch` query values.

A staged artifact with a flipped byte fails `verify()` with `HashMismatchError`; with a correct hash but a signature from an unknown key fails with `SignatureError`; with valid hash and signature passes; in both failures the temp file is deleted and the installed binary is byte-identical.
Verification happens before apply in every code path: an `apply()` call on an unverified StagedUpdate throws `NotVerifiedError` (tested by calling apply first).

Interrupting a 50 MB download at 40 % and calling `download()` again resumes with a `Range` request and ends with a verified file; a server sending more bytes than manifest `size` aborts at size+1 byte.

Apply on a SEA fixture directory replaces the binary atomically (the old file is never partially written: a simulated crash between steps leaves either the old or the new file complete) and `centcom.prev` exists; `rollback()` restores it; the downgrade without `--rollback` is refused.
On npm and Homebrew install methods `apply` is not performed and the command prints the matching upgrade command (`npm i -g ...` / `brew upgrade ...`) with exit 0.
Background check runs at most once per 24 h (state file), makes no request when `CENTCOM_NO_UPDATE_CHECK=1`, and a failing/slow endpoint (> 5 s) never delays startup or fails the command.
A `client_too_old` response or WS close 4426 sets `required:true`; `centcom update --check --json` prints `{available, version, channel, required}` and exits 10 when available.
Manifest failing schema validation, or listing no artifact for this platform/arch, produces a clear 'no update for this platform' result and no download.
No log line or error contains the signed URL query string.
tests: update/verifier.test.ts: hash and signature matrices with test keys, key rotation (two keys), wrong key id, malformed signature.
update/downloader.test.ts: resume, size cap, timeouts, abort, progress.
update/applier.test.ts: atomic replace with injected fault points, rollback, Windows-style rename path via fs fake.
update/checker.test.ts: semver/channel rules, required flag, 24 h throttle, opt-out.
update/install-method.test.ts: detection per install layout fixtures.
update/cli.test.ts: flags, exit codes, JSON output in the pty harness.
guardrails: MUST verify SHA-256 and the Ed25519 signature against the embedded public keys BEFORE touching the installed binary; MUST NOT apply, execute or even chmod +x an unverified file.
MUST NOT fetch public keys from the network or accept keys from the manifest; the trusted key set is compiled in (and MUST support rotation with two active keys).
MUST download only over https (except an explicit test base URL) and MUST NOT follow redirects to non-https hosts; MUST enforce the manifest `size` as a hard cap.
MUST apply atomically (same-directory rename) and keep one previous version for rollback; MUST NOT leave a half-written executable on any failure path.
MUST NOT self-modify package-manager installs (npm, Homebrew); MUST NOT require elevated privileges silently: if the install dir is not writable, print the manual instructions.
MUST NOT downgrade or switch channel without an explicit flag; MUST NOT block startup or any command on update checks.
MUST NOT log signed download URLs or signatures beyond the key id.
failure_modes: Network drops mid-download -> keep the partial file, resume next time (partial files older than 7 days are deleted); never apply a partial.
Install dir read-only -> report `NotWritableError` with the exact manual steps; nothing changed.
Manifest signature infrastructure rotated to a key the client does not know -> `SignatureError` with advice to reinstall from the website; no unsigned fallback.
Disk full during staging -> remove temp file, report the needed space.
New binary fails a post-apply `--version` smoke check -> automatic rollback to `centcom.prev`.
notes: Manifest fields (artifact url, sha256, size, signature, min_client_version, notes url) come from schemas/release-manifest.schema.json, which is not present in the contracts/ snapshot.
